acceptance_criteria.criterion: After a sort click, the search input field retains any leading or trailing spaces the user typed.
Pressing Tab moves focus to each sortable column header in DOM order; pressing Enter or Space on a focused header triggers the sort (same behaviour as a click).
The sort indicator arrow appears on the active column when navigating by keyboard.
String column sort order (project, repository, status) is identical across browsers with different default locales.
All previously verified sorting AC (original WP-001/WP-002 AC 1–15) continue to pass unmodified.

summary: Fix 1 (search trim leakage): Added searchRaw closure variable; restore input uses searchRaw, handler captures raw value before normalising.
Fix 2 (keyboard accessibility): Added tabindex="0" and role="columnheader" to thSort() output; added delegated keydown listener on thead mirroring click logic with e.preventDefault() on Space.
Fix 3 (localeCompare collation): Changed bare localeCompare(bStr) to localeCompare(bStr, 'en', { sensitivity: 'base' }) for deterministic cross-browser string sort.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. All three fixes follow existing patterns (delegated listeners, closure variables, ES5 syntax constraint maintained throughout).

summary: AC 1 (search trim leakage): searchRaw closure variable introduced at L247; searchEl.value = searchRaw on restore (L426); searchRaw = this.value captured before normalization (L428). Correct.

AC 2 (keyboard sort): tabindex="0" and role="columnheader" in thSort() at L305. Delegated keydown listener on thead at L394 mirrors click handler exactly; handles Enter and Space; e.preventDefault() for Space prevents page scroll. Correct.
AC 3 (sort indicator on keyboard): render(allProjects) called after keyboard-triggered sort; thSort() rebuilds th with .sort-asc/.sort-desc class on the active column. Indicator updates correctly.
AC 4 (localeCompare collation): aStr.localeCompare(bStr, 'en', { sensitivity: 'base' }) at L275. Correct and deterministic.

AC 5 (no regressions): All three changes are additive. closest() at L397 follows the pre-existing pattern already used in the click handler (L376, L380) — not a new API. No logic changes to applyFilter(), sortProjects() numeric paths, or table rendering beyond the targeted lines.

comments.note: No bugs found. closest() usage in the new keydown handler (L397) follows the identical pattern already established in the pre-existing click handler (L376, L380) — consistent and correct. ES5 syntax constraint upheld: no arrow functions, const/let, classes, or template literals introduced.

e.target.closest('th[data-sort]') in the keydown handler correctly handles the case where a th has tabindex="0" and receives focus directly — e.target IS the th, so closest() returns it immediately. No off-by-one or bubble issue.

summary: Reviewed all three targeted changes in mcp-server/gui/public/app.js. Fix 1 (search trim leakage, L247/L426-429): searchRaw closure variable introduced alongside searchValue, correct restore order (value set before listener attached), raw value captured before normalisation. Fix 2 (keyboard accessibility, L305/L394-410): tabindex="0" and role="columnheader" are correct ARIA attributes; delegated keydown listener on thead mirrors click handler exactly; e.key === ' ' with e.preventDefault() correctly prevents page scroll; e.target.closest('th[data-sort]') is safe because focus lands directly on the th. Fix 3 (localeCompare, L275): locale 'en' and sensitivity 'base' are correct choices for deterministic, case/accent-insensitive alphabetical sort. All fixes are additive, contained within the renderProjectList closure, and maintain ES5 syntax throughout. No regressions introduced. All 5 AC confirmed.

comments.note: The sort-toggle logic block (6 lines: key comparison, sortDir assignment, localStorage writes, render call) is duplicated verbatim between the click and keydown handlers (L379-392 and L399-410). Not a defect — extraction to a shared named function would eliminate the duplication, but this is a minor maintenance note given the ES5 no-module constraint.

sensitivity: 'base' in localeCompare makes 'a', 'A', and 'à' sort equivalently. This is the right choice for a project name list but worth documenting in a code comment for future maintainers who may not know why the option was added.
